assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a minimal nonlinear stochastic model that organises kinetic roughening, growth fronts and many interface problems into one universality class with exact exponents in one dimension. It is the clean, general mechanism that statistical physics aims for, and later exact solutions (random matrices, integrability) and experiments tie it to random-matrix theory.
assessment.attribution: The 1986 paper is by Kardar, Parisi and Zhang. Only Kardar and Zhang are available among the credited names here. Spohn is credited for the mathematical and exact-solution programme, not the original proposal, so a prize built on the discovery itself would fit Kardar and Zhang best, though the absence of Parisi from the supplied names is a real gap in a fair configuration (Parisi already shares the 2021 prize, which complicates matters).
assessment.maturity: Nearly four decades old. Exact one-dimensional solutions (Johansson, Prahofer-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel, Sasamoto-Spohn) and clear experiments on liquid-crystal turbulence (Takeuchi-Sano) give independent confirmation of the Tracy-Widom statistics. Timely and mature.
uncertainties: Parisi is not among the credited names, so the original three-author credit cannot be reproduced.
Experimental realisations in the strict KPZ class are few and sometimes debated.
Credit for the later exact solutions is spread over many mathematical physicists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active matter statistical physics brings an entire non-equilibrium class under a field-theoretic description: the Vicsek model shows a flocking transition, and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamics shows long-range order in two dimensions that is forbidden in equilibrium. Ramaswamy's work on active hydrodynamics and polar and nematic fluids supplies a third foundational pillar. The ideas are simple, general and travel across biology, soft matter and robotics.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek (1995 numerical model), Toner and Tu (1995 to 1998 hydrodynamic theory and renormalisation-group analysis) and Ramaswamy (active gels, hydrodynamics, 1998 onward) are all decisive, and the three-way split is natural and fits the supplied names well. Other contributors (Marchetti, Cates, Tailleur, Bechinger) lie outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Theory is well established; quantitative experimental confirmation of the Toner-Tu scaling is still patchy, and the field is still moving fast. Recognition is reasonable but could be seen as slightly early compared with older universality results.
uncertainties: Direct quantitative tests of Toner-Tu exponents are limited.
Priority and breadth questions between the numerical model and the continuum theory, and the roles of other leaders in active hydrodynamics, may arise.
Whether the committee regards the field as sufficiently consolidated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming transition provides a unifying, geometric picture of rigidity onset in disordered solids (granular matter, foams, emulsions, glasses). The isostatic point, critical scaling and the link between marginal stability and soft vibrational modes constitute a mechanism that is simple and widely applicable, and it has stimulated a large interdisciplinary literature.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 'jamming phase diagram' and later work with O'Hern, Silbert and Langer on point J, plus Wyart's isostaticity arguments and marginal-stability analysis, are the core. The three credited names make a plausible set, although O'Hern, Silbert and Durian are important in the numerics and are not available.
assessment.maturity: Strong numerics and many experiments, but the theoretical picture (mean-field, replica results from Parisi, Zamponi and others in infinite dimensions) is still evolving, and the relevance of the critical picture to finite-dimensional glass remains debated.
uncertainties: Relation of jamming to the glass transition is not settled.
Credit is shared with simulation collaborators and with mean-field theorists outside the credited names.
Experimental verification of criticality in real granular systems is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator concept opened a major field: topologically protected edge and surface states with spin-momentum locking. The 2005 Kane-Mele proposal and the 2007 experimental realisation in HgTe wells are a textbook case of theory followed by decisive experiment, and the concept has generalised widely.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theoretical identification, Molenkamp's group delivered the first observation (with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal providing the HgTe route, and BHZ and Zhang are not in the supplied credit list). The three credited names are a sound but imperfect configuration, since Zhang's contribution (and Fu, Moore and Balents for 3D) would need to be weighed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and 3D materials by ARPES; mature and widely accepted. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz, which does not cover this discovery.
uncertainties: BHZ and later three-dimensional topological insulators bring crowded credit.
Quantitative edge-conduction in 2D realisations remains imperfect.
Overlap with earlier prize themes may be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1984 BPZ construction of conformal field theory gave exact solutions for two-dimensional critical phenomena: infinite-dimensional Virasoro symmetry, minimal models and exact critical exponents. This is an extraordinary example of universality made precise, with direct consequences for statistical mechanics, string theory and quantum field theory.
assessment.attribution: Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov wrote the foundational paper, and the three credited names exactly match it. Zamolodchikov (the Alexander B.) is alive and Polyakov is also alive, while whether Belavin and Zamolodchikov remain eligible should be checked (I am not certain about current status of all three), which affects feasibility.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with validation in the Ising, Potts and tricritical Ising models and in numerics and experiments, and with decades of confirmed impact. Recognition would be long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Eligibility and health of the laureates should be verified, and I cannot independently confirm it.
Whether the committee views this as mainly mathematical or theoretical rather than physical discovery.
Overlap with Polyakov credit in other candidates on the longlist.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters and have made the Mott insulator, superfluid transition, and strongly correlated dynamics experimentally accessible, including single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes. They provide the quantum simulator idea with a clean connection to statistical mechanics.
assessment.attribution: Greiner (Mott transition 2002 with Hänsch and Bloch, and the quantum gas microscope), Bloch (broad programme) and Esslinger (fermionic Hubbard physics, Mott insulator of fermions) are decisive experimentally. Zoller (with Jaksch) made the original theory proposal and is also a strong candidate, and with four credited names the choice is a real trade-off. Leaving Zoller out is a defensible but costly decision.
assessment.maturity: Mature, independently reproduced in many laboratories. Since a prize to the BEC pioneers in 2001 and to the 2012 and 2022 quantum optics laureates, there is some risk of seeming repetitive.
uncertainties: Whether the theory proposal by Jaksch and Zoller should be recognised.
Open question of whether simulation of truly new many-body regimes has been demonstrated beyond classical computing.
Overlap with already recognised cold-atom topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a theoretical flat-band prediction into an experimental platform for correlated insulators, superconductivity and topological moiré states, so that interaction physics can be tuned by twist angle. The idea is simple, general and has created a whole field of moiré materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle (2011), and Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered the correlated insulator and superconductivity in 2018. The three credited names express that theory-plus-experiment pairing well, though Cao and Fatemi (students) and Dean's, Kim's and Yacoby's groups made parallel contributions.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups worldwide, but the origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states remain under debate. Recognition may be somewhat premature for a field only about seven years old.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is not settled.
Sample-to-sample variation and reproducibility concerns early on.
Credit for student-level discoveries and for the parallel groups could be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model and confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking, using detectors and analysis on an unprecedented scale. The importance and clarity of the discovery are beyond doubt, although my own field expertise lies elsewhere.
assessment.attribution: The theory was recognised in 2013. The experimental credit lies with large collaborations, so any individual configuration is arbitrary. The credited names include spokespeople (Gianotti, Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) and the LHC accelerator leader (Evans). I choose the proposers of the detectors, which is imperfect, and I acknowledge that cutting from five names to three would be contentious.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with extensive subsequent coupling measurements. Prize recognition for the experiment has been delayed by the attribution problem rather than a lack of evidence.
uncertainties: Fair attribution to a collaboration of thousands within the rule of three.
Whether the accelerator contribution (Evans) should outweigh a detector pioneer.
Outside my core expertise, so I defer to colleagues on particle physics.
